videos.script: Until now every image came from somebody else. This lesson builds one, for Ana's own service. {{project}} First the service itself: six small files you create once and keep for the rest of the course. The program reads its settings from the environment, logs where Docker collects it, and stops when it is told to. {{file}} Six lines are enough: a base image, a folder, a copy, a compile, a port and a command. {{build}} The build prints one numbered step for each piece of work, and the program answers on her machine. {{signals}} Then one line changes, and stopping the container takes ten seconds instead of a fifth of one. The difference is whether a shell sits between Docker and the program. {{args}} Then build arguments and environment variables: one lives during the build, the other in every container. {{context}} And last, the context. Docker sends the whole folder to the builder, and a password file ends up inside the image. One small file keeps it out.
